coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Humboldt Street Plaza
record.summary: Planned small, mostly paved flexible-use plaza between Blocks 4 and 9 at the foot of Humboldt Street, giving a car-free connection from Delaware Street to the Blue Greenway and a waterside Bay overlook terrace (D4D 4.24, 4.19.2). A Phase 2 open space due before the first certificate of occupancy for the building representing 3 million sq ft of development; no design review or construction has been reported.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- Figure 6.2.3 labels this open space directly, shown as a small plaza area between Block 4 (north) and Block 9 (south). This polygon is a simplified rectangular approximation of that labeled area, built directly from Block 4 and Block 9's own already-committed corners (see digitization_method) so it shares an exact edge with both -- its accuracy now tracks whatever those two files carry.
notes.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (p.245).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Open space with no subdivided Assessor parcel of its own within the largely unaddressed former power-station site. (This is our own parcel-search narration, not something the cited Design for Development can establish; the D4D does not address Assessor parcels.)
notes.regulatory_context: A small public plaza per the D4D's own Figure 6.2.3 label, between Block 4 and Block 9 near the site's waterfront edge.

facts.value: California Barrel Company LLC (project sponsor); now Fifth Space (formerly Associate Capital)

'open and flexible space, primarily paved', for open-air markets, performances, public art and interpretive exhibits; required amenities: seating, lighting, open flexible-use plaza space, planted areas, bicycle parking, waste receptacles, power for temporary markets and performances; 26-foot emergency vehicle access between Blocks 4 and 9 from Delaware Street
Block 4 (north) and Block 9 (south); waterside Bay Overlook Terrace at Humboldt Street Plaza continues the plaza paving across the Blue Greenway (D4D 4.19.2)
Phase 2 (DA originally Phase 1); delivered before the first certificate of occupancy for the building representing 3 million sq ft of total development

IMP: 26-foot fire access for 150 feet from Delaware Street and 20-foot emergency access to the waterfront; sits over a public utility easement; conceptual stormwater outfall at Humboldt Street Plaza (IMP Figure 15.4); overland release option where streets meet the plaza
Owned and maintained by the Project Master Association (IMP 9.2)

open_questions: No acreage for Humboldt Street Plaza is stated in the D4D, DEIR, IMP, DA recitals, Phase 1 application or annual reports; the geometry is a rectangle between Blocks 4 and 9 without a sourced area.

No design review application, cost, or construction date exists in any source; the plaza is a Phase 2 item behind a 3-million-sq-ft occupancy trigger that no source dates. The earlier expected-completion milestone (2031, from SocketSite's Oct 2020 Phase 2 window) was replaced on 2026-09-29 because that 2020 forecast has not held (as of Sept 2026 no Phase 1 market-rate building has started) and the Port's Nov 2025 memo says open space is tied to vertical development expected over the next 10-15 years.
The interim Prequel Park (Power Station sub-area polygon in the repo) shares edges with this plaza; whether the interim park occupies the plaza's footprint is not shown in any scaled drawing on file.
BOS File 260724 (Amended and Restated DA, 2026) amends the Phasing Plan; possible changes to this plaza's phase were not checked (draft DA not read).

No designer of Humboldt Street Plaza is named in any source found: in the final D4D, CMG Landscape Architecture appears only as a photo credit on precedent images (Figure 4.24.4 and elsewhere), not as the plaza's designer, and no design review application exists for the plaza.
